sentences.text: Llukalkan is a small abelisaurid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina.
Its estimated body length reached 3.95 meters.
This animal possessed a unique air-filled cavity in the middle ear region not seen in other members of its group.
Scientists formally described this new taxon in 2021.
The generic name translates to one who scares in Mapuche, while the specific name means different skull in Latin.
Researchers classify Llukalkan as a derived abelisaurid within the clade Furileusauria.
It lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 86.3 to 83.6 million years ago, in what is now South America.
The validity of Llukalkan was initially questioned because its holotype was found in the same area and time period as Viavenator remains.
